_comment: Gold set parsed from bisociation-domain-pairs.md — Koestlerian reconstructions of generative-relation transplants. Used as few-shot exemplars for bisociation mode (COA 2). Not claimed quotations; operational form: relational rule X also governs Y.

pairs.first_person_sentence: “If populations outrun resources, then those with advantageous variation will leave more descendants; scarcity turns variation into selection.”
“If the X-ray pattern reveals the molecule's geometry, then the geometry should tell us how hereditary information can be physically stored.”
“What Faraday sees as lines of force, I can express as a mathematical field; the physical intuition becomes a set of equations.”
“A bicycle is unstable until I control it; an airplane should be no different—the problem is not merely flying, but steering the instability.”
“If an economy transforms matter and energy just as an engine does, economic production must obey physical constraints too.”
“A message can be represented as discrete symbols, and discrete symbols can be manipulated as logical states.”
“What if strategies compete the way organisms compete? Then fitness can select among behaviors.”
“An option price evolves like a diffusing quantity; if the mathematics of diffusion applies, finance can inherit the machinery of physics.”
“Evolution does not know the answer; it searches by variation and selection, so an algorithm can do the same.”
“A market is not just a collection of prices; it is a game in which each player's best move depends on everyone else's.”
“If the water rises by exactly the volume I immerse, then displacement is geometry made physical.”
“Put the Sun at the center, and the strange planetary motions become patterns I can describe with simple laws.”
“Fermentation is not merely chemistry happening on its own; microorganisms can be the agents producing the chemistry.”
“The continents fit like pieces of a larger object; perhaps the map is not fixed—the land itself has moved.”
“If traits are inherited in discrete units, Darwin's selection suddenly has something concrete to select.”
“If Maxwell's light speed is invariant, then space and time must adjust rather than light violating the equations.”
“If the thermal spectrum refuses continuous energy, perhaps nature itself trades energy in discrete packets.”
“If simple local rules can generate complex patterns in a machine, perhaps biological form can emerge from simple rules too.”
“The thermostat regulates temperature by feedback; an organism does the same thing with its internal state.”
“A grammar is a rule system, and rule systems can be computed; language therefore has a machine-like structure.”
“The solution does not always emerge by accumulating attempts; sometimes the whole pattern suddenly reorganizes.”
“If inheritance is probabilistic, Darwinian selection can be described mathematically as changes in gene frequencies.”
“A strategy can be stable not because players consciously choose it, but because variants using it cannot be invaded.”

pairs.insight: Theory of the firm / Coase theorem
pairs.first_person_sentence: “When using the market costs something, the boundary of the firm becomes an economic solution to the cost of transacting.”
“Capitalism evolves by destroying old forms and selecting new ones; innovation is economic mutation under competition.”
“No one possesses all the knowledge needed to coordinate an economy, but prices can carry fragments of that knowledge.”
“The uncertainty in a message behaves mathematically like entropy; information can therefore be measured as the reduction of uncertainty.”
“Nature solves problems without a designer, so computation can imitate nature's search through variation and selection.”
“If price changes resemble random motion, then the mathematics of Brownian motion can price financial claims on that motion.”
“Players choose against one another, but resources constrain them; equilibrium can emerge from strategy operating under scarcity.”
“If the water rises exactly as much volume as I immerse, then displacement is geometry made physical.”
“The press already stamps grapes into wine; why not use the same pressure to stamp letters into pages?”
“The body has hidden structure like a machine, and perspective gives me a way to make that structure visible.”
“The heart behaves like a pump; therefore blood should move in a circuit rather than simply disappear into the body.”
“Treat matter like money: whatever enters the chemical ledger must leave it somewhere.”
“If gases mix in measurable proportions, perhaps matter itself is composed of discrete units.”
“Equal volumes under equal conditions should contain equal crowds, even when the crowds are made of different molecules.”
“A heat engine is really a machine for moving heat between temperatures, and that movement has a limit.”
“If breeders can accumulate traits by choosing parents, nature can accumulate traits by determining who reproduces.”
“Railroads move bodies along tracks; wires can move messages along tracks at nearly instantaneous speed.”
“The telegraph carries coded symbols electrically; perhaps speech itself can become the electrical signal.”
“A lightbulb becomes a technology only when I solve not just the bulb, but the factory and network that make millions of bulbs useful.”
“If alternating currents create a rotating field mathematically, perhaps that field can rotate a machine physically.”
“If a signal can cross space as a wave, then the wire was never essential to the message.”
“The contaminant is not merely ruining my culture; it is killing bacteria, and that killing may itself be useful.”
“A bicycle stays upright by controlling its instability; a flying machine must solve the same problem in three dimensions.”
“The slaughterhouse moves the carcass past the worker to take it apart; I can move the automobile past the worker to put it together.”
“A worker's motion can be measured like a machine's motion; therefore work itself can be engineered.”
“A supermarket replaces what customers have taken; the factory should replace what production has consumed.”
“A neuron either fires or does not fire; that makes it look remarkably like a logical switch.”
“When two neurons repeatedly act together, their connection should become the physical trace of that cooperation.”
“If a neuron can add weighted inputs and decide whether to fire, it can classify patterns.”
“A neural network can settle like a physical system into a low-energy state, and that state can be a memory.”
“The error at the end can be traced backward through every dependency, so calculus can tell every connection how to change.”
“Instead of programming the correct action, let the machine discover good actions from reward and punishment.”
“If real people systematically violate the model of rational choice, psychology belongs inside economics.”
“People cannot calculate everything, so real decision-making must be understood as computation under limits.”
“Understanding a situation may mean activating a structured mental frame, much as a program loads a data structure.”
“Evolution does not know the answer; it searches a space by varying, recombining, and selecting candidate solutions.”
“If evolution can search for useful organisms, evolution can search for useful programs.”
“Let the optimizer behave like matter cooling: explore widely while hot, then settle into a good configuration.”
“If nature computes with quantum states, perhaps a computer should compute with quantum states too.”
“Erasing a bit is a physical act, so deleting information must carry a thermodynamic cost.”
“Order need not fight entropy; energy flowing through a system can create structure.”
“A tiny difference in atmospheric conditions can become a huge difference later; predictability therefore has a mathematical limit.”
“The irregularity of markets resembles the irregularity of natural fractals; perhaps prices have structure across scales.”
“A pile can organize itself to the edge of collapse without anyone deliberately tuning it there.”
“A molecule that specifies how another molecule is built is behaving like an information-bearing code.”
“Genes are not merely instructions; they can switch one another on and off like a control circuit.”
“What looks like one organism may actually be a coalition of organisms that became inseparable.”
“Helping a relative can still spread my genes; reproduction need not stop at my own body.”
“Helping another can be adaptive when today's cost buys tomorrow's return.”
“Let strategies compete over repeated games, and cooperation itself can evolve.”
“An organism cannot be understood by isolating its parts; the relations among the parts constitute the whole.”
“Cities scale like organisms: changing size changes the way infrastructure and social activity behave.”
“Millions of speakers generating language independently still produce a striking statistical order in word frequency.”
“Wealth is not distributed like a bell curve; a small number possess a disproportionately large share.”
“The household is an economy too: time, labor, children, and consumption are resources to be allocated.”
“A commons is not inevitably tragic; its users can create institutions that regulate the resource together.”
“Technologies do not compete on merit alone; an early advantage can compound until history itself selects the winner.”
